newsitem.title: POLAND: Plock oil refinery to invest in southern Poland.
newsitem.headline: Plock oil refinery to invest in southern Poland.

text.p: Poland's biggest refinery, slated for privatisation, plans to invest in the south of the country to boost sales, Petrochemia Plock's spokeswoman said on Thursday.

Romana Kuffel told Reuters that Plock, which signed a letter of intent this week to buy the small Trzebinia refinery in the industrial region of Silesia, also planned to lay a pipeline to the southern city of Wroclaw and build a fuel terminal there.
The new pipeline will run from the company's headquarters in the central city of Plock.
The refinery also plans to extend by 100 km an existing pipeline to link the Plock facilities and the Trzebinia refinery, Kuffel said earlier in a statement.
Construction will be carried out together with the state-owned oil pipelines' maintenance firm PERN, Kuffel said.
She said the investments are designed to increase Plock's sales in the southwestern Poland, where about 40 percent of Poland's petrol is sold.
Plock is being prepared for privatisation by state-owned holding Nafta Polska SA, which has been given its shares.

Nafta is to offer 30 percent of Plock's shares this year to strategic investors, a stake which could later be increased to a controlling on the condition that investors implement their investment pledges.
Under the government's oil sector privatisation scheme, an investor in Plock is to get access to the lucrative network of state-owned CPN's 1,400 filling stations.
